 :JUDGMENT:

This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 16.02.2024 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of T.B. Shiva Shankarappa due to the impact of the accident.
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2075/2024 2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:

It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased Shiva Shankarappa who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 16.02.2024 due to the negligent parking of the driver of the respondent's lorry.

It is submitted that on 16.02.2024 at about 5.15 a.m., deceased Shiva Shankarappa was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-KH-9601 slowly, carefully following traffic rules and regulations wearing helmet and when he reached near Gnanabharathi school, Hesaraghatta main road, at that time, the respondent's lorry bearing Reg.No.RJ-29-GA-9895 was parked in center of the road without warning signboards, hazard lights as a result Shiva Shankarappa dashed to the lorry, resulting in the accident.

sentences.text:
Immediately after the accident Shiva Shankarappa was shifted to Prakriya hospital,
but he died while under treatment on 24.02.2024.

Consequently, on 16.02.2024 a FIR No.0011/2024 was registered with the Chickabanavara Traffic Police station under SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2075/2024 Sec.283 and 337 of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.283 and 304(A) of IPC against the driver of the lorry.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the negligent parking of the driver of lorry.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 48 years and working as priest at temple and also working as a driver and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m. and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12%
p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 has remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending lorry bearing Reg.No.RJ--29-GA-9895 in SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2075/2024 favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.1 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said lorry did not have valid and effective driving license.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the negligent parking of the driver of the lorry.
It is submitted that the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
The age, avocation of the deceased is denied.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. Vide order dated 29.05.024 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. T.B. Shiva Shankarappa S/o Basavarajappa was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 16.02.2024 at about 5.15 a.m.,
near Gnanabharathi School, Hesaragghatta main road, Bengaluru, due to negligent parking of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.RJ-29- GA-9895 in the center of the road without taking precaution by its driver?

sentences.text: 3 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri. T.B. Shiva Shankarappa?

3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
4) What Order or Award ?
5.

In order to substantiate the claim petition, the claimants have examined petitioner No.1 as PW1 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 18.
6.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2075/2024 respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent parking of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.RJ-29- GA-9895 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle).

8. In this regard the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and in her chief-examination she has deposed that on 16.02.2024 at about 5.15 a.m. while the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KH-9601 wearing his helmet at that time offending lorry parked in the center of the road without any precautions in negligent manner and the motorcycle collided with the parked vehicle, resulting in the accident and death of the motorist.
In support of the same, the petitioner No.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 which is FIR registered under Sec.283 and 337 of IPC on the basis of Ex.P2 complaint.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P3 - spot mahazar and sketch which shows accident spot which is at the center of the road towards Hesaraghatta which shows that offending vehicle has not parked at the side of the road.

In addition Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2075/2024 offending vehicle, wherein it is clearly mentioned that the offending vehicle was parked without any precautionary measures and in violation of traffic rules on the middle of the road and the accident has taken place due to negligent parking of the driver of the offending vehicle.

9. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is subjected to cross-examination except the suggestion that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased himself nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to disprove the manner of the accident.

Hence, in Anitha H P vs Meenu Jain on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165062401/
4 the absence of any rebuttal evidence it can be concluded that the accident took place due to negligent parking of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the "Affirmative ".
10. Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Shiva Shankarappa.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P14 to 17 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners and deceased.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2075/2024 and the deceased.

Hence, they have a right to apply for compensation due to death of Shiva Shankarappa in RTA.
11.

In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.

entities.text: Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Reliance can also be placed on the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020), wherein it was expounded that "major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not."
12.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Shiva Shankarappa have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Shiva Shankarappa and also they have proved that the death of the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2075/2024 Shiva Shankarappa has been caused by negligent parking of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads

is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 48 years.
Ex.P-14 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 20.05.1974.
The alleged accident has taken place on 16.02.2024.
Hence, by considering Ex.P14, the age of the deceased is taken as 50 years.
14. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a priest at temple and also working as driver with Dr. Roshanchandra Shetty and was earning Rs.35,000/- per month.
In this regard, PW.1 has produced Ex.P9 - SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2075/2024 letter.
But PW.1 has not examined the author of Ex.P9.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,500X 12= 1,98,000/-.

Hence for the purpose of computation of Anitha H P vs Meenu Jain on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165062401/
5 claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,98,000/-.

sentences.text: 15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in these decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the Point of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2075/2024 (i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 25% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self - employed and was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

16. The petition discloses that petitioner no 2 and 3 are the major daughter and son of the deceased and hence they cannot be considered as dependents of the deceased by virtue of the judgment in SLP (Civil) Nos 22265-22266 of 2018 between Deep Shikha & Anr Vs National Insurance company Ltd and Ors.

entities.text: Deep Shikha & Anr Vs National Insurance company Ltd and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the petitioner No 1 alone is to be considered as dependent of the deceased and entitled for loss of dependency.
The petitioner No 2 and 3 on the other hand are only entitled for compensation for loss of estate and consortium.
17. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife and daughter and son.
Hence while calculating the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2075/2024 deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was pleased to hold that where the sole dependent of family,  of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
18. In this Petition, the deceased was aged 50 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 25% of the income has to be added.
So, 25% of Rs.16,500/- comes to Rs.4,125/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.20,625/- p.m. (Rs.16,500/- + Rs.4,125/- =
Rs.20,625/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 13.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to hold that where the sole dependent of family,  of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

19. After deducting  of the income towards his personal SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2075/2024 expenses in Rs.20,625/- it comes to Rs.10,313/- (Rs.20,625/- - 10,312/-) and multiplier applied is 13,
(Rs.10,313/- x 12 = 1,23,756/-, Rs.1,23,756/- x 13 = 16,08,828/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,08,828/- towards loss of dependency.

The petitioners have produced Ex.P11 - Medical bills total 25 in nos. and hence the petitioners are entitled an amount of Rs.3,69,258/-

21. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2075/2024 case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

sentences.text: In view of the foregoing reasons and discussions, the petitioners are entitled compensation amount of Rs.21,59,586/-.
22. Regarding rate of interest:

As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

entities.text:
SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

23. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the negligent SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2075/2024 parking of the driver of the offending lorry bearing Reg.No.RJ-29- GA-9895.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
24. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,59,586/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.21,59,586/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2075/2024 date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
